CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke Announces Return to India for Peaceful NEET Protest.

Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the satirical social media platform Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), has announced his return to India on June 6 to lead a peaceful protest in Delhi demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal.

The Third Seat View: This development marks a fascinating shift from digital satire to real-world political mobilization, tapping into deep-seated youth frustration over systemic educational failures. While the government views the rapid rise of the CJP with suspicion, citing potential foreign backing and initiating digital crackdowns, the movement's undeniable resonance highlights a massive trust deficit between students and public testing institutions.

⭐Cockroach Janta Party Storms Jantar Mantar — June 6, 2026⭐

Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), landed in Delhi early Saturday morning and headed straight to Parliament Street Police Station to seek protest permission. Police granted permission and the demonstration at Jantar Mantar began shortly after.

Thousands of young supporters gathered at the iconic protest site, carrying national flags and books, demanding the immediate resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over repeated paper leaks in NEET-UG, CUET, SSC GD and CBSE examinations.

Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk also joined the protest, stating — "If not us, who? If not now, when?"

Heavy security was deployed across the area. Several students alleged that police pressured them not to attend, though authorities denied the claims.

The CJP movement was born on May 16, 2026, after India's Chief Justice compared unemployed youth to "cockroaches and parasites." Within days, the movement exploded to over 20 million Instagram followers — turning an insult into a revolution.

Today, that online revolution hit the streets.

Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), has demanded the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged exam-related lapses, including NEET-UG paper leak concerns and CBSE on-screen marking issues.

Targeting the Centre during a protest at Jantar Mantar, he questioned accountability and said, “If accountability is not getting fixed, it is the responsibility of the Prime Minister Narendra Modi to take the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.” He also added, “If he can stop the war between Russia and Ukraine, can’t he stop the paper leak?”

Dipke warned of a nationwide agitation if the demands are not addressed within a week.

Source: ANI

Meet Ujjwal 🌻

• You may have already seen him online being trolled and targeted with derogatory slurs like Meetha, Chakka, Hijda, and worse.

• Ujjwal is a 19-year-old queer person who has just passed his Class 12 exams.

• He may have no connection whatsoever to the NEET paper leak controversy, yet he still showed up at the Jantar Mantar protest organized by the Cockroach Janta Party.

• He understands the pain and frustration of the 22 lakh students and their families affected by the paper leak, as well as the millions of others who have suffered because of more than 89 major exam paper leaks across the country.

• As a queer individual fighting for his rights, visibility, and existence in a deeply transphobic and homophobic Indian society, he has likely faced immense struggles himself. Yet despite that, he chose to show up for others.

• He may have participated in protests before too, something that many educated and socially aware people never do in their entire lives.

• From these videos, one thing is clear: he has a great sense of style and carries himself with confidence.

• He is socially aware, respectful, politically conscious, and unafraid to speak about rights, justice, and issues that matter.

• Meanwhile, lowlifes hiding behind fake profiles chose to mock and ridicule him for doing something I would call an act of genuine courage.

• He is far better than the self-proclaimed internet sigmas, alphas, and low-testosterone junglees who are just a burden on society, freeloading on government freebies and spreading hatred online. They are the reason for India's bad reputation globally, not someone like Ujjwal.

• If we had more Ujjwal, people who are aware, confident, educated, and bold enough to challenge a corrupt system. We might have saved thousands of students, women, farmers, LGBTQIA+ people, soldiers, and countless others who lost their lives while fighting for justice.

• And Ujjwal, if you're reading this: we see you. We appreciate you. We love you.

Thank you for showing up when it mattered.

Sending hugs. 🫂❤️

P.S. I apologize for any accidental misgendering or for using incorrect pronouns while referring to him.

सत्ता के अहंकार में डूबी मोदी सरकार अब इस मुकाम पर पहुँच गई है कि अपने अधिकारों, निष्पक्ष परीक्षाओं और सुरक्षित भविष्य की मांग करने वाले छात्रों को ही शिक्षा मंत्री “आतंकवादी” कह रहे हैं।

ज़रा सोचिए - जिसकी नाकामी से इतने पेपर लीक हुए, जिसके राज में 20 बच्चों ने जान दे दी, जिसने करोड़ों युवाओं का भविष्य अंधेरे में धकेल दिया - वो आज पीड़ित बच्चों और उनकी आवाज़ उठाने वालों को “दहशतगर्द” बता रहा है। 

पर यह कोई नई बात नहीं: अन्नदाता किसानों को "आंदोलनजीवी और परजीवी" कहा। सवाल पूछने वाले को “Anti-National” कहा। और अब युवाओं को “दहशतगर्द।”

जो भी सरकार से सवाल पूछे - उसे देशद्रोही बता दो, यही इनकी पूरी राजनीति है।

धर्मेंद्र प्रधान जी, देश के करोड़ों युवाओं से तुरंत माफ़ी माँगिए और अपनी नाकामियों के लिए इस्तीफ़ा दीजिए।

और रही मेरी बात - आप मुझ पर जितने चाहें हमले कर लीजिए। मैंने कोटा में कहा था, और फिर कहता हूँ: यह शिक्षा व्यवस्था आज सिर्फ़ एक वसूली तंत्र बन गई है। मैं इसे ऐसे ही नहीं रहने दूँगा।

हर बच्चे को सस्ती, अच्छी शिक्षा और निष्पक्ष परीक्षा मिले - इस आवाज़ को उठाना मैं कभी बंद नहीं करूँगा।

#ChhatraJodo

Dharmendra Pradhan, in a TV interview, called the "Cockroach Janta Party" (CJP student/youth protest group) the "B-team of terrorists" and accused Rahul Gandhi of trying to "spread terrorism" by meeting protesting students in Kota. Congress frames it as the minister labeling students terrorists.

Context: NEET-UG 2026 canceled after confirmed paper leak (guess paper overlaps); CBI arrested several. Multiple leaks reported over years (70-90+ in a decade per some data).

Student suicides: Reports cite at least 11-12 recently linked to the controversy/re-test stress (figures vary; Kota coaching pressure is a long-term issue). Rahul cited ~20.

Exam integrity failures are real and serious. The rhetoric is heated political sparring on both sides. Students need accountability and fair systems, not labels.

This isn’t some harmless sit-down at Jantar Mantar anymore. The infection is spreading.

What began as the “Cockroach Janta Party” meme born from a CJI remark and weaponised on social media. It found its breeding ground in the NEET paper leak.

And the contagion has already reached the Supreme Court. We saw it with our own eyes when a young man stood there and hurled abuses. This is no longer protest. This is a deliberate, organised attempt to radicalise every disgruntled and dissatisfied youth, turn them against the country, against our institutions, and against India itself.

The slow poison is working. Time to call it what it is.
@rahulroushan nailed it.

body:
I want to take a moment to thank Abhijeet Dipke.
For 19 days now, he has been teaching this nation a masterclass.

Not in exam reform.
In something more valuable.

He flew in from Boston. Unemployed.
To save India's students.

Then handed the mic to Allah.
Kashmir.
RSS.
Umar Khalid.

Wait.
Where is Dharmendra Pradhan?

Well. 
He is not generating any TRP.
And he is having fun continuing as Education Minister.

Turns out the fastest way to save a minister's job is to hire professional protestors.

Pradhan should be sending flowers to Jantar Mantar.
Maybe Pradhan hired Abhijeet Dipke.

Nobody even remembers his name is on the placards anymore.

Special mention to Sonam Wangchuk.
Came for a guest appearance.
Stayed to become the whole show.

19 days without food. Visibly.
While everyone else on that stage eats on schedule.

And the menu is incredible.

Continental on Monday.
Chinese on Tuesday.
Hyderabadi on Wednesday.
American on Thursday.
Repeat.

With desserts.
Tea.
Coffee.

Imagine fasting for 19 days next to a buffet you're not invited to.

Every speaker walks up.
Says a few lines about Allah.
Ambedkar.
Kashmir.
RSS.
Umar Khalid.
Then walks off to eat.

Wangchuk stays.
Hungry.
Foolish.
Watching.

Wondering if anyone even remembers what this started as.
At some point even the most patient man starts doing math.

If Wangchuk could speak freely right now. 
Off the record.
We suspect it would not be about the education ministry.
It would be about catering.

Here's the real service Dipke has done this country.
He has finally taught us how to spot a cockroach.

Not the ones NEET aspirants are competing against for a medical seat.
The ones standing on a stage at Jantar Mantar.

Holding a mic.
Talking about everything except the paper leak that started this.
And still don't know who is President of India.

The real students are indoors.
Revising.
Silent.
Unheard.
The stage belongs to everyone else now.

So thank you, Abhijeet Dipke.
You didn't get Pradhan to resign.
You got India to forget why he should.

That takes talent.

Popularity isn't evidence, and dissent isn't immunity. 

My point was never that people can't protest, it's that the conversation has shifted from the students who were wronged to the personality leading the headlines. 

That's political theatre, not accountability, Dr. Sharma. Everyone knows why CJP was formed, why it occupied Jantar Mantar, and the kind of slogans that echoed there.

No one is disregarding the real anguish of the NEET aspirants and families whose years of hard work were destroyed by this leak and the authorities' repeated failures. But they deserve more than this activist led spectacle. 

Rather than this Wangchuk, more of the people must come out and protest.
empty fasts and selective outrage won't deliver that.

The government met members of the satirical political group Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) after they held a protest in central Delhi today, sources said. The CJP has been demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG paper leak.

The group's spokesperson @SauravDassss in a post on X said that he and another spokesperson, @AshutoshRanka, met Union minister JP Nadda at his house for 10 minutes.

"While we submit a written letter with our demands, he has assured us that he will meanwhile speak internally. We are in that process..." Das said. "The minister assured us he will discuss this at the appropriate level. However, no commitments have been made so far. The peaceful protesters will not rest until the demand is met."

He also shared a copy of the letter on X.

Arundhati Roy has repeatedly stated that Kashmir is not a part of India and that the Indian Army has forcibly occupied it. If you organize a protest with the support of such individuals, majority of the people will not support your cause.

Shabana Azmi also appeared at Jantar Mantar, is associated with Christian NGOs whose objective is to convert Hindus. Slogans such as "Naam Rahega Allah Ka" are also being raised.

If such activities are intended to create unrest or disorder in the country, then, in my view, any action taken by the administration or the police including the lawful use of force to protect India's integrity would be justified.

🇮🇳|The University of Delhi, the crown jewel of India's education system, issued a cowardly advisory on Thursday. It told students to "stay away from Jantar Mantar." It warned of "legal action, academic consequences and safety risks."

JNU followed suit on Friday, urging students to "act responsibly" and "prioritise their personal safety."

The regime's message was clear: stay in your rooms. Stay out of the streets. Stay silent.

But the students of DU had a different message.

As a Response...they gathered at the Arts Faculty. Not in thousands but in spirit. Not with permission but with purpose.

They became the voice that the Chancellor, a bootlicker of Modi and the RSS, tried to silence.

They carried the pain of NEET aspirants who died by suicide.

They carried the memory of students lathi-charged, tear-gassed, and detained.

They carried the demand that Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan must resign.

And they carried something else: the refusal to be intimidated.

The Gen-Z movement has spread beyond Jantar Mantar. It has entered the classrooms, the hostels, the corridors of power. The regime can close 17 metro stations. It can cut the internet. It can deploy 45 battalions. It can issue a thousand advisories. But it cannot stop a generation that has decided: we will not stay away.

The Chancellor of DU bent the knee to the regime. The students bent the arc of history.

To every student at DU who stood up: you are not alone. You are the voice of a nation that refuses to be silent. And you will not be forgotten.✊🏻🇮🇳

I first met @AshutoshRanka two months ago, when the NEET paper leak controversy had just erupted, well before the CJP was formed. He had painstakingly compiled data on every major paper leak in India over the last two decades and sent it to me on WhatsApp. The research was meticulous and deeply impressive.

Little did I imagine that this same young engineering graduate would soon be sitting across the table from two Union ministers, negotiating on behalf of student protesters.

As he told me, he had never even been to Jantar Mantar before this. Ashutosh isn’t a professional agitator. He’s an idealistic young Indian who chose to act.

I interviewed him last night after the CJP-government talks. He looked exhausted, seemed unwell, but spoke with remarkable clarity and conviction.

If there’s one lesson from the last few weeks, it’s this: never underestimate the power of informed, idealistic youth. You don’t have to agree with everything Ashutosh says but cannot but admire his spirit. Watch: https://t.co/81PxIP0Izo

Jantar Mantar Agitation Withdrawn as Centre Accedes to Key Demands! 
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has officially announced the end of its multi-week protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar following the third round of high-level negotiations with a central government delegation comprising Union Ministers J.P. Nadda and Jitendra Singh.  Speaking at a joint press conference, CJP National Spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka confirmed that the agitation was called off after the government accepted its core demands, starting with the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. In addition to the minister's exit, the Centre agreed to:
- Withdraw all FIRs and legal cases registered against protesting students and organizers, guaranteeing no future retaliatory action.  
- Provide maximum financial compensation under regulatory provisions to the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide amid the examination controversy.  
- Consider the 5-point charter on examination system reforms submitted by the student leaders.  
- CJP spokespersons urged all student protesters to vacate the venue peacefully and return home as the government pledged to honor its commitments in good faith.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday welcomed the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, calling it a victory for public pressure and issue-based politics.

Addressing supporters at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, Dipke said the development showed that governments could be held accountable when people united over public concerns instead of religious divisions.

18-year-old NEET aspirant Sharim allegedly died by suicide on 13 June following the alleged NEET-UG paper leak controversy. A resident of Amarpur village in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district, Sharim had been preparing for NEET at Aakash Institute in Jasola, Delhi.

His elder brother, Firoz Qureshi, says he has been seeking justice ever since. According to Firoz, he first approached the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), requesting that Sharim's photograph and details be displayed on the protest stage, but alleges that his request was ignored.

Firoz further claims that on 15 June, he went to Shaheen Bagh Police Station to file a complaint, but alleges that the police did not take his concerns seriously.

According to Firoz, he made one final attempt on the last morning of the Jantar Mantar protest to raise his brother's case with CJP representatives, but says he was once again ignored.

Will Total Filth, Vulgarity, And Abuse Qualify As Protest? 

We pose a crucial question to the country: Can utter filth, vulgarity, and insults ever be deemed an acceptable form of democratic protest? After our extensive investigation into the significant devastation and heaps of waste left at Jantar Mantar by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), we are now revealing the alarming behavioral truth of these so-called student leaders.

Is concealing oneself behind the facade of NEET-UG student protests a justification to use insults, employ crude language, and bluntly disregard the laws and regulations of the nation? We challenge the apologists and the hypocritical group that relentlessly supports this complete collapse of civic sense. Here is the direct, unfiltered footage that highlights the harsh slogans and the shocking behavior of the demonstrators. The constitutional assurance of peaceful protest exists in this nation, but does that revered right allow for public vandalism and offensive language?

Observe and determine for yourself, is this the promised youth revolution for the country, or merely a politically driven crowd disguising its motives behind authentic student concerns? 
We demand the arrest of Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dahiya for a start. They’re working against the government, the country, killing the progress and development, vandalising national property and beating up the Police force in Delhi. The judiciary needs to be strict and should come down hard on these anti India elements working against our nation, disrespecting our Hon’ble Prime Minister and the cabinet, if the judiciary doesn’t act this will become a normal practice for anti social elements.
Credit : Republic Media Network.

PM Modi himself posted a series of selfie-style videos on Instagram in recent days, thanking youngsters for their response and suggestions on issues such as examination reforms.

In the news today, another Cockroach protest on the horizon? Chargesheet filed in NEET paper leak case, Indian sailors trapped in Ukraine war, and more.....

Cockroach Janta Party now threatens a protest against the Supreme Court order

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Tuesday, July 28, stated that the Supreme Court's interim order permits authorities to continue investigating FIRs registered during the nationwide student protests. The so called party says that the order was contrary to the assurances given by the Centre during negotiations that ended the protests at Jantar Mantar.
“The Supreme Court has now said that FIRs that were already registered will not be withdrawn. This is not what was discussed in our negotiations with the government,” CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said.
CJP has threatened another protest if the order is not withdrawn.

_____________________________________________________

Govt rolls out 'One Officer, One Official Car' rule to curb misuse, cut spending

The government has rolled out a new “One Officer, One Official Car” policy aimed at curbing the misuse of government vehicles and reducing unnecessary expenditure. Under the new rule, officials will be assigned a designated official vehicle instead of multiple cars being used by the same officer or department.
The move is expected to improve accountability, optimise the use of government resources and bring down spending on fuel, maintenance and vehicle operations. It also seeks to discourage the practice of government vehicles being used for personal or non-official purposes.
___________________________________________________

CBI files chargesheet against 13 accused in NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has filed a chargesheet against 13 accused in connection with the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case, marking a major development in the investigation into irregularities surrounding the medical entrance examination.
The chargesheet reportedly details the alleged roles of the accused and the conspiracy through which the question paper was leaked and subsequently circulated among candidates. The case has raised concerns over the integrity of competitive examinations and the security of the examination system.

____________________________________________________

13 Indian sailors trapped in the Black Sea near Ukraine amid attacks

Thirteen Indian sailors are reportedly trapped in the Black Sea near Ukraine amid ongoing attacks and heightened security concerns in the region. The sailors are believed to be facing difficulties as military activity and strikes have disrupted maritime operations, raising concerns about their safety and ability to leave the area.

The situation has drawn attention to the risks faced by seafarers operating in conflict-affected waters. Authorities are expected to monitor developments closely and explore options to ensure the sailors’ safe evacuation or passage to a secure location.

_____________________________________________________

Pakistan’s Defense Minister Khawaja Asif defends the killing of protestors in Pakistan-Occupied-Kashmir, says they are enemy like India

Pakistan Occupied Kashmir has been seeing widespread protests for weeks. Islamabad has unleashed unheard of brutality on the protesters, killing them with impunity. Despite the barbarity of the establishment, the protest is only growing.

Now, Pakistan’s Defense Minister Khawaja Asif has tried to justify the murders of the protesters by saying that they are enemies like India.

Notably, he had earlier said that these protesters in Pakistan Occupied Kashmir aren’t even real Kashmiris.

Arnab Goswami issues a direct and powerful call to the government: The officials must swiftly apprehend, charge, and not show leniency towards those concealing themselves behind the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) facade!
